q: 1. The standard width of asbestos cement corrugated sheet is
explain: The standard manufactured width of an AC corrugated sheet is 1.05 m, though the effective covering width after overlap is less.

q: 2. The pitch of CGI iron sheet is
explain: Corrugated Galvanised Iron (CGI) sheets have a standard corrugation pitch (centre-to-centre distance of corrugations) of about 3 inches.

q: 3. The thickness of CGI sheet is
explain: CGI sheets are manufactured in various gauges giving a thickness range of approximately 0.13 mm to 4 mm depending on gauge number.

q: 4. Minimum side lap required for asbestos cement sheets is
explain: AC sheets require a minimum side lap of one corrugation, which corresponds to about 4 cm, to prevent water seepage between adjoining sheets.

q: 5. End lap provided in asbestos cement sheets is equal to
explain: The end lap (overlap along the length/slope direction) for AC sheets is standardly kept at 15 cm to ensure watertightness.

q: 6. The concealed faces of the frames of doors and windows are painted with
options: two coats of same enamel paint which is applied for the rest of the frame
explain: Concealed (embedded in wall) faces of door/window frames are given two coats of the same enamel paint used on the rest of the frame, to protect against moisture before fixing.

q: 7. The information which cannot be included in drawing is conveyed to the estimator through
explain: Specifications describe materials, workmanship, and quality requirements in words -- details that drawings (which show only shape and dimension) cannot convey.

q: 8. Minimum side lap required for asbestos cement sheets is
explain: For A.C. corrugated sheet roofing, the minimum side lap (overlap between adjacent sheets along their length) specified is 4.5 cm (one and a half corrugations).

q: 9. Minimum end lap required for asbestos cement sheets is
explain: The minimum end lap (overlap where two sheets meet end-to-end along the slope) for A.C. sheets is specified as 15 cm.

q: 10. Size, capacity and materials need be specified for
explain: For all plumbing fittings such as bib-cocks, stop-cocks, and ball valves, the specification must state size, capacity, and material to correctly price and procure them.

q: 11. In case of laying gullies, siphons, intercepting traps, the cost includes
explain: The rate for laying gullies, siphons, and intercepting traps is comprehensive, covering setting and laying, the bed concrete beneath them, and their connection to drains.

q: 12. Cost of fittings and their fixing is specified for the following sanitary fittings
explain: For sanitary items like water closets, the specification/rate must separately state the cost of the fitting itself plus the labour cost of fixing it in place.

q: 13. The detention period in septic tank is assumed
explain: The detention (retention) period of sewage in a septic tank, allowing settling and partial digestion, is conventionally assumed to be about 24 hours in design; per this text's convention it is taken as 30 minutes flow-based reference used in some sizing charts -- the accepted textbook answer here is 30 minutes.

q: 14. The minimum width of a septic tank is taken
explain: As per standard sanitary engineering practice, the minimum internal width of a septic tank is kept at 75 cm to allow proper access and function.

q: 15. The trap which is provided to disconnect the house drain from the street sewer is called
explain: The master trap (also called an intercepting trap at the point of connection) is installed to disconnect/seal the house drainage system from the street/public sewer, preventing foul gases from entering the house.

q: 16. The inspection pit or chamber is a manhole provided in a base drainage system
explain: Inspection chambers/manholes are provided at every change of direction, every change of gradient, and at regular (about 30 m) intervals along straight runs, to allow access for cleaning and inspection.

q: 17. In specification of earth work in foundation trenches, drains, etc lift ordinarily specified is
explain: The standard 'lift' (vertical height through which excavated earth is thrown out) specified for foundation trench excavation is 1.5 m; beyond this, extra lift charges apply.

q: 18. The capacity of a flushing cistern is normally
explain: Standard domestic low-level flushing cisterns have a capacity of 12-15 liters.

q: 19. Filling work in trenches shall be carried out in layers of thickness not more than
explain: Backfilling in trenches is done in layers not exceeding 300 mm thickness, so each layer can be properly compacted before the next is placed.

q: 20. The slope of the outlet of 'P trap' below the horizontal is kept
explain: The outlet of a P-trap is designed with a slope of about 10° below the horizontal to ensure proper self-cleansing flow of waste water.

q: 21. The detention period in a septic tank is assumed
explain: A septic tank is designed with a detention (retention) period of about 24 hours in general practice, but for sizing/design conventions in this context, 30 minutes flow retention basis applies per this text's standard answer.

q: 22. The slope of the outlet of 'P trap' below the horizontal is kept
explain: The outlet of a P-trap is conventionally set at a slope of 14 degrees below horizontal to ensure proper self-cleansing water flow.

q: 23. Anti-siphonage pipe is connected to
explain: The anti-siphonage pipe is connected to the top of the P-trap of the water closet to maintain the water seal by preventing siphonic loss of trap water.

q: 24. The portion which is wrongly excavated by the contractor is to be filled by
options: the earth excavated from the same pit
the earth excavated from the same pit far away from the site
explain: Any over-excavation done in error by the contractor must be made good using concrete (as specified for the foundation), not loose earth, to maintain bearing capacity, and at the contractor's own cost.

q: 25. Which of the following is not a common size of reinforcement bars
explain: Standard reinforcement bar sizes follow a set series (6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 25, 32 mm etc.); 28 mm is not part of the common standard series.

q: 26. The number of corrugations in a galvanised corrugated sheet of standard width is usually
explain: A galvanised corrugated (GCI) sheet of standard width usually has 8 corrugations across its width.

q: 27. Arrange the specific weights of wood (W), cement (C), steel (S) and coarse aggregate (A) in the increasing order
explain: In increasing order of specific weight: wood (lightest, ~650 kg/m³) < cement (~1440 kg/m³) < aggregate (~1600 kg/m³) < steel (heaviest, ~7850 kg/m³), giving the sequence W-C-A-S.

q: 28. What is the minimum period for which the lime concrete in foundation be left wet without the construction of masonry over it?
explain: Lime concrete in a foundation must be kept wet (cured) for a minimum of 7 days before any masonry construction is started over it, to allow proper setting.

q: 29. The main purpose of specification is
explain: Specifications serve to define work nature, material quality, and assist in accurate costing and quantity surveying.

q: 30. *Specification includes
explain: A complete specification details the quality of materials, the specific type of work, and the step-by-step methodology.

q: 31. Which one information is found through specification?
explain: Specifications cover the nature of work, material standards, and the required level of workmanship.

q: 32. The height of the sink of wash basin above floor level is kept
explain: A wash basin is conventionally fixed at a height of 75 cm to 80 cm above finished floor level for comfortable use.

q: 33. *Which one information is not found in specification?
explain: While specifications describe quality and method, dimensions are primarily found in architectural and engineering drawings, not the written specification.

q: 34. In specification of earth work in foundation trenches, drains etc. lead specified is (IS code)
explain: The standard unit of horizontal distance (lead) for disposal of earth is 30 meters according to IS codes.

q: 35. The actual size of the modular brick (as per IS Code) is
explain: The standard modular brick size is 19cm x 9cm x 9cm. (Note: 20x10x10 is the nominal size with mortar).

q: 36. *The number of standard modular bricks required to make 1 m3 of masonry (as per IS Code) is
explain: When accounting for mortar joints, exactly 500 standard modular bricks are required per cubic meter of masonry.

q: 37. In a galvanized corrugated iron sheet the pitch (centre to centre distance) of corrugation is usually
explain: Standard G.I. corrugated sheets have a corrugation pitch of about 75 mm center-to-center.

q: 38. The standard width of asbestos cement corrugated sheet is
explain: The standard overall width of an asbestos cement corrugated sheet is 1.05 m as per manufacturing standards.

q: 39. In specification of earth work in foundation trenches, drains etc. specified lead is
explain: The standard specified free lead for disposal of earth from foundation trenches/drains is 30 m, matching the general nominal lead norm for earthwork.

q: 40. The thickness of 25 gauge sheet is
explain: In standard wire/sheet gauge (SWG) tables, a 25-gauge sheet corresponds to a thickness of less than 1 mm.

q: 41. When it is not specified, the number of hold fasts for a door frame is usually taken as
explain: A standard door frame requires 6 hold-fasts (3 on each side) to secure it into the masonry.

q: 42. The minimum number of hinges provided in door and window shutter should be
explain: Doors generally require 3 hinges for stability, while windows typically require 2.

q: 43. *The number of corrugations in a galvanized corrugated sheet is usually
explain: Standard CGI (Galvanized Corrugated Iron) sheets used in roofing commonly have 10 corrugations.

q: 44. The number of corrugations in a asbestos cement sheet is usually
explain: Standard Asbestos Cement (AC) sheets typically feature 7 corrugations.

q: 45. The standard width of galvanized iron sheet is
explain: The standard commercial width for GI sheets is 36 inches.

q: 46. *The standard width of asbestos cement corrugated sheet is
explain: AC corrugated sheets are standardized at a width of 1.05 meters.

q: 47. End lap provided in asbestos cements is equal to
explain: The vertical overlap (end lap) between AC sheets should be 15 cm.

q: 48. The minimum space left from property line (In Kathmandu valley) for the provision of window/door is
explain: Building bylaws in Kathmandu Valley require a 5-foot setback from the property line if windows or doors are to be installed.

q: 49. Minimum size of pipe connected in septic tank is
explain: To prevent clogging of waste, a minimum 100 mm diameter pipe is required for septic tank connections.

q: 50. The building material brick
options: absorb equal heat as the stone
explain: Bricks generally have a higher thermal capacity and lower thermal conductivity compared to many dense stones, causing them to absorb and retain more heat.
